description: Figure 9 is a bar chart illustrating the effect of context masking perturbations on probing accuracy, broken down by part-of-speech tag. The horizontal axis lists different syntactic or lexical categories—such as “NOUN,” “VERB,” “ADJ,” “ADV,” “PROPN” (proper noun), and others—arranged in descending order of the magnitude of the perturbation effect. The vertical axis represents the effect size, expressed as a percentage of the original unperturbed accuracy, ranging from approximately -10% to +30%, with tick marks at 5% intervals. Each bar corresponds to a specific tag and shows the average effect of masking its context on model probing performance, with error bars extending vertically to indicate the standard deviation across trials or models. The bars vary in height: “PROPN” exhibits the largest positive effect (around +25%), indicating a substantial drop in probing accuracy when proper nouns are masked, while “VERB” shows a much smaller effect (near 0%), consistent with the text’s observation that verbs are less affected. Some bars, such as “ADJ” and “ADV,” show small positive effects (around +5–10%), while “DET” and “PRON” show near-zero or slightly negative effects, suggesting minor improvements in probing accuracy under perturbation. The chart visually emphasizes that proper nouns are most vulnerable to context masking, supporting the claim that models rely heavily on contextual cues for these items, especially in morphologically rich languages.
